prelude: Derrick Berg (14 years old). He was only introduced in the after credits scene of episode 10, but he’s actually really important for later stuff. He comes from the City of Silver, which the clues Klein collects point to its existing in the Forsaken Land that many people had been looking for. His people speak Jotun, an ancient language that was spoken by giants before their extinction (above the gray fog, Klein, a historian proficient in ancient languages, uses the fog for real-time translation, making the others understand Derrick’s words), and they worship a being referred to as either “The City of Silver Creator” or “The Ancient Sun”, believing he had abandoned them but would return if they were pious enough.

The Forsaken Land is stuck in an eternal darkness, with their only source of illumination being the neverending lightning storms. They needed to always have lanterns lit as the darkness contained 2 types of danger: monsters that appear all of a sudden, and the dark itself, which caused people who stay a few seconds in it to just disappear as if they were erased from existence.

As a place that was separated from the rest of the world after the Cataclysm in the Second Epoch, the City of Silver preserved a lot of ancient history that the rest of the continents didn’t know about. They also carried out explorations of the land but only ever found ruins, believing they were the last humans left alive. They also suffered from a curse: if someone died without being killed by a blood-relative, they would mutate into a dangerous monster. Derrick’s first appearance was when he had to kill his parents as they approached the end of their lifespan.

The lack of sunlight and living creatures (other than monsters) meant that they lacked food, with the only edible thing around them being Black-Faced Grass. Other than that, they could eat monster corpses, but too much of it would cause their bodies to become deformed. The people there are also extremely tall, like Derrick is already 1.9 meters or something at this point in the story, with people on the Giant pathway being even taller.

He had only ever read about the sun and the moon in books, so he wanted to be the sun that illuminated the way ahead for his people, protecting them from all danger. That was why he chose The Sun as his tarot card and got the Bard potion formula through the Tarot Club (that’s Sequence 9 of the Sun pathway). As the Forsaken land is completely disconnected from the rest of the world, he could only ever exchange knowledge, not materials.

She had a noble friend around her age named Viscount Glaint. They were both deeply interested in mysticism and wanted to become Beyonders, so, when he finally met one, he also introduced her to Audrey. That Beyonder was named Fors Wall, a famous writer who often interacted with the nobles and signed books (a mystery and romance novel she wrote, titled “Stormwind Mountain Villa”, gets brought up a lot, everyone in the LOM world has read it), she was a Sequence 9 Apprentice (they could pass through doors and thin walls, she also carried a mystical item that allowed her to teleport a limited number of times, with her being able to gain that ability permanently if she could advance her Sequence).

Fors later introduced Audrey to her friend and roommate, Xio Derecha, a Sequence 9 Arbiter. Xio’s family was once considered noble before her father was accused of something and they fell from grace, she had since been investigating with the hopes of mending her father’s reputation and providing for her mother and younger brother. The two of them were very involved with Beyonder circles and had a lot of resources that could help Audrey collect ingredients and information.

This arc started when Alger issued a mission in the Tarot Club to kill this pirate vice-admiral, who possessed a mystical item called Creeping Hunger: it could save and use 1 to 3 of the powers of up to 5 Beyonders that have been “Grazed” by it (their characteristic was devoured, yes the item, which was shaped like a glove, had a mouth). The only powers I currently remember are: one which allows the user to transform into anyone, and I think he had powers similar to a Nightmare, maybe also some from the Spectator pathway.

Qilangos had been preparing to assassinate a noble named Duke Negan, so he snuck into a ball after having changed his appearance. There, he bumped into Audrey who, as a Spectator, noticed small oddities in his behavior (she had previously gotten Xio and Fors to investigate him and his habits), instantly informing The Fool that she may have found Qilangos. Klein then informed The Hanged Man and even sent a letter to Mr. Azik for help. Qilangos was unsuccessful in his mission but, as he tried to run away, he was easily finished by Azik in a terrifying manner. He then left with Creeping Hunger, with Alger arriving alongside the Church of Storms to only find Qilangos’ corpse. Audrey, who had saved Duke Negan by warning her father that one of the nobles was acting in an odd manner, received a huge reward, hoping to give part of it to The Fool’s “Blessed” who got rid of the pirate.

The emotional outcome of this was that Audrey became very proud that their secret organization had become capable of carrying out missions like that, while Alger was terrified that The Fool had someone this powerful “working under him”.

Near the end of Volume 1, Audrey had owed Klein some money. Wanting to keep his identity a secret, he went to a bank that allows for the creation of an anonymous account and set his password as The Fool’s Honorific Name. That way, if anyone ever tried anything, he would be able to hear them. Audrey sent the money over and then, not long after, the final battle against Megose happened. Seeing as Klein was only able to rise from the grave without having the chance to retrieve any belongings, it was only thanks to this anonymous bank account and the money he hadn’t yet withdrawn that he would be able to start a new life in Backlund.

214: In the evening after his stunt as a Clown, Klein arrived using a steam locomotive to Backlund, the most prosperous capital in the Northern and Southern Continents with a population exceeding five million people. One of the city’s defining features was its yellow smog indicating the heavy pollution in the air, limiting visibility and obscuring the sun. Klein was even surprised at it only being half past six, stating it looked like it was nine or ten.

He also mentioned the establishment of organizations like the Soot Reduction Association and Smoke Reduction Association, and the passing of a bill stating the need to establish the National Atmospheric Pollution Council.

Klein thought about the fact that not being constantly aware of the exact time made him feel a sense of horror (weirdo, reminds me of myself) which had led him to buy a pocket watch, but instead of a silver one to match his temperament, he opted for a gold one to match the true essence of a Clown: being “showy” and “exaggerated”.

He took a sudden turn, causing a person who was tailing him to lose sight of his target (that person was an average thief, idk why I mentioned it since there are no repercussions), then stopped to check the map he had bought. That morning, he had concluded the true essence of a Clown: “Although being capable of knowing a little about fate (as a Seer), one remains helpless towards fate; therefore, one might as well use a smiling face to hide all the pain, sorrow, confusion, and depression.”

He could feel a bit of his potion digesting, so he started narrowing down his choices for obtaining his sequence 7 formula: The Secret Order seldom appeared. He could start making contact with local Beyonder circles for clues, or set a trap using his knowledge of the Antigonus family’s treasure and that mysterious symbol (shown to him when a puppet opened Tingen’s Chanis Gate). The biggest issue was his fear of attracting the attention of the Order’s leader, Zaratul, who could even guide Roselle and may or may not still be alive.

After eliminating the areas strongly associated with the Church of Evernight, the poorer districts, and anywhere that would require identification (which, as a recently deceased person, he had no identification), Klein took a second-class seat on a metro to Cherwood Borough. Before the metro set off, he saw an adolescent boy mistakenly take the second-class carriage before apologizing and heading to the third-class one. Not long after, a group of men boarded Klein’s carriage, seemingly looking for the boy. Klein ignored them, after all, it was none of his business (for now).
215: Arriving at Minsk Street, Klein found the residence of Stelyn Sammer, who was renting out another Unit she owned. The Madam was in her thirties with blonde hair and blue eyes, her living room was nearly equivalent to the entire Moretti’s first floor in area, and from future interactions, I can tell you right now that she loved to brag about her wealth and class. Her husband, Luke Sammer, was a manager at the Coim Company, and a member of the Loen Kingdom’s Soot Reduction Association.

Klein introduced himself as Sherlock Moriarty and internally mocked the woman for how many details about her life and family she was willing to share with someone who just did not care. They reached an agreement and he paid a deposit of half a year’s rent (she had originally wanted a contract for the entire year, but Klein didn’t know when he’d have to abandon everything and be on the run, so he refused), before going to check out his new house. After settling down, he started considering what job he could have: it had to be something lucrative so he wouldn’t suffer financially, but it couldn’t be something that would restrict him and affect his movements.

He thought of becoming an author by plagiarizing (like Roselle), but his sensitive identity (a dead person) made him wary of becoming famous. He also considered becoming a news reporter, but job applications required documents that he didn’t have on hand and had no way of forging for the time being. In the end, he settled on becoming a private detective.
216: Klein posted an advertisement for his identity as a private detective in a newspaper unique to Backlund, as he had no way to offer his services elsewhere. On his way back, he bought various herb powders and silver slices and later prepared all of the mysticism essentials he had to keep on him.

His current plans were to focus on what he could gain from the Tarot Club, along with his own advancement. He could also use his career to get in touch with many different people and slowly find clues regarding the Secret Order. He wouldn’t seek out Ince Zangwill yet, as the gap in their powers remained too great for Klein. But if he did run into the man, he wouldn’t have minded sending an anonymous letter to the Church. Aside from that, Klein wanted to find a suitable starting business to invest in.

When it was almost time for the Gathering, Klein took four steps counterclockwise and headed above the gray fog, ruminating over the fact that this was one of the few things in his new life that hadn’t changed. He warned The Sun Derrick Berg, who was resting while on patrol with his team. The boy found a calm place to sit and pretended to be asleep.

After all three members were summoned, The Hanged Man Alger Wilson said that he had obtained 19 pages of Roselle’s diary, but he could only give 6 pages at a time, as that was the limit to his memory. The first was about re-making contact with “that pathetic fellow trapped in the storm”: he called himself Mr. Door and promised to fulfill three of the emperor’s requests if he helped him escape. Roselle refused to help but listened to the man’s teachings about the Fourth Epoch.
217: The page gave insight into the “War of the Four Emperors”, which involved the Black Emperor of the Solomon Empire, the half-insane Blood Emperor of the Tudor Dynasty, the Night Emperor of the Trunsoest Empire, and the Emperor of the Underworld of the Southern Continent, also known as Death. Most of the emperors fell one after another, with Death reaping the greatest benefits. He later went mad but also became stronger, teaming up with the Primordial Demoness to bring about a Pale Disaster for the Northern Continent.

It also mentioned the Law of Beyonder Characteristics Indestructibility and the Law of Similar Sequence Beyonder Characteristics Conservation, things Roselle had already learned of in a “most secret and ancient” organization he was part of. He wrote how, if there were too many High-Sequence Beyonders in a pathway, the number of Low-Sequence ones would reduce and vice-versa.

All this information pushed Klein’s mind to the bleak conclusion that madness was an inevitability if one lived long enough, causing him to smile to hide the solemnity of his emotions. He turned his thoughts to the Black Emperor whom the original Klein had studied, believing the title to be the name of that pathway’s corresponding sequence 1.

He felt that the laws mentioned contradicted reality; as the Churches had many artifacts and HighSequence Beyonders, while Low-Sequence Beyonders still ran rampant. He wondered if the destruction of the Nation of Evernight could’ve been a solution when it came to the Evernight pathway, or perhaps certain Sealed Artifacts could have been used for potions.

The second page had Roselle complaining about the pathway he had chosen, noting how it lacked any combat abilities up to Sequence 5 and going into detail about Sequences 9 to 6, comparing them to 7 and 6 of the Mystery Pryer pathway and lamenting over the fact it was incomplete and had a powerful evil being named the Hidden Sage presiding over it.
218: The third page had some thoughts about the beginning of the rebellion in Intis and ended on a cliffhanger: Zaratul, the leader of the Secret Order, had come to visit Roselle. But the subsequent pages had nothing to do with this entry, leaving Klein frustrated. The turmoil described reminded Klein of Roselle’s death six years after he had declared himself Emperor. The half-historian believed his death hid more than what appeared on the surface, and that it had power struggles between Beyonders behind it, unlike what was taught in textbooks.

The rest of the pages didn’t have anything important, the last of them just ended with Roselle sending someone to investigate the Secret Order, with the findings remaining unknown to Klein. Having been done reading, The Fool mentioned the two laws to the members of the gathering, only explaining the first one: Beyonder characteristics can’t be destroyed, only passed on. After a Beyonder dies, their characteristic can be used to make a mystical artifact or as the main ingredient of their Sequence’s potion, without the supplementary ingredients. Alone, it can be used as a half-mystical object.
Justice Audrey Hall was horrified by this knowledge, but the other two seemed to already know it. As for the explanation of the second law, Klein wasn’t going to give it for free.
219: The Hanged Man, who believed the Fool to be an ancient, powerful entity who recently reawakened and was working to break free of his confines, along with Justice, agreed to help gather information regarding the Secret Order, while the Sun had already been owed from a previous deal.

Klein explained how some pathways are exchangeable at High-Sequences, giving an example of the Death pathway’s Sequence 5 being able to advance normally or to the Giant (now known as Gatekeeper) pathway’s sequence 4. This reminded Derrick of the City of Silver’s former chief, who had retreated into a mausoleum he had built for himself. The young boy suspected he was trying to switch from the Giant pathway to the Death pathway, implying the City of Silver didn’t have the subsequent formulas for their sequence 4. Though that chief’s complete disappearance implied his failure.

The Fool refused to say what other pathways were exchangeable until information about the Secret Order was collected (he didn’t know any more, the readers already should though thanks to the ending of Volume 1). After that was over, Klein asked Audrey and Alger to cooperate with him in an attempt that would help them exchange materials through him, without needing to reveal their real identities to one another.
220: The Fool described how one side would prepare a sacrificial ritual aimed at him, with the other preparing a bestowment ritual using regular and Beyonder materials as test subjects. The only requirement was for them to draw the symbol he showed them (the one behind his chair), then chanting his name along with a few lines in ancient Hermes or Jotun.

The Hanged Man internally wondered why the Fool was using them for these trials instead of his “Blessed”, but he never dared to voice these concerns out-loud, believing that there were secrets he didn’t know and that the Fool’s Blessed was being monitored. They all agreed to make the attempt as soon as the gathering was over.

Afterwards, Audrey mentioned her knowing of two Beyonders with their own circles and resources in Backlund, believing them to be suitable members for the Tarot Club. Klein hesitated as he had initially wanted his organization’s members to remain anonymous so that, if any one of them was ever caught, they wouldn’t be able to divulge information about the others, but her mention of Beyonder circles caught his interest.

In the end, he told her that they would need to pass certain “examinations” before joining, but she first had to find a discreet method to get them to recite his Honorific Name (The Fool that doesn’t belong to this era, the Mysterious Ruler above the gray fog, the King of Yellow and Black who wields good luck). With the end of that week’s gathering, the three members returned to the real world while Klein remained above the gray fog, awaiting the attempt.
221: Alger successfully sacrificed the ingredient, growing more fearful at the Fool clearly becoming more and more powerful, though he was consoled by the fact that he was one of the earliest members of their secret organization, so the Fool probably wouldn’t cause him any harm once he became strong enough to enter the real world.

Above the gray fog, Klein examined the ingredient in his hand, feeling proud of the success of his idea. He then sent it to Audrey once her ritual was ready. The young noble immediately used the ingredient to prepare her potion and drank it, successfully becoming a Sequence 8 Telepathist.

Returning to the real world, Klein bought gold-rimmed glasses, wigs, and a variety of mustaches, he also rented a small apartment in East Borough, the poorest district of the city, so he would always be ready whenever he needed a disguise or to escape a difficult situation. He spent the next two days experimenting with the gray fog and crafting charms, with his bell finally ringing on Thursday.
222: The ringing of the bell made Klein worry that clients could come looking for him while he wasn’t home, making him lose business. He thought of putting a notice board whenever he went out, or doing a divination at the beginning of every day before deciding to leave. His premonition as a Clown allowed him to see the visitors before he opened the door: they were an old lady and a young man in his twenties.

They were Mrs. Doris and her grandson Jurgen Cooper, a senior solicitor. They lived on the same street as Sherlock Moriarty and had wanted to entrust him the mission of finding her cat, Brody, who had gone missing the previous night. Klein, who was a bit disappointed at his first job being “find a cat”, eventually agreed, so he followed them to their home to start gathering clues.

Finding a few strands of black fur, Klein used his cane for Dowsing Rod Seeking. Following the direction it pointed to, he opened a cupboard. The cat was in a cupboard in their house, it never left. When asked how he knew Brody’s location, Klein’s answer was: “Deduction, my good man.”

Returning to his house, he found someone waiting at his front door: it was the adolescent boy from the metro (refer to the end of chapter 214). Being invited inside, the boy introduced himself as Ian, informing Klein that he recognized him as the man who was sizing him up that day. Ian explained that he had been hired by a detective named Zreal Victor Lee to gather information, which led to the scene on the metro.

After that encounter, Zreal disappeared, with his home having indications of being infiltrated. The boy tried reporting the situation to the police, but it hadn’t been long enough yet, and other detectives refused the mission, saying they had just seen the man at gatherings. That led him to seek the help of someone unfamiliar to both him and the detective.
223: Observing the young boy, Klein reached the conclusion that he had never come into contact with Beyonders or mysticism before, which was why Ian believed that: 1) it couldn’t be possible for someone to fool detectives by acting as Mr. Zreal, 2) he was being forced by someone. The task he had for Klein was to just investigate and determine the man’s condition, without any further action. They settled on a small payment in advance and Ian owing three favors after the task was done, with the boy promising he’d appear at the right time so the detective won’t have to contact him.

As he paid, Klein determined that Ian must suffer from OCD because of the way he carefully arranged the money. The boy left and Klein divined whether the case involved Beyonders. The divination failed to give results.

That night, Klein, disguised as a regular worker, observed Zreal’s empty home. He divined that there was danger, but nothing serious. Sneaking in, his Spirit Vision showed three people lying in ambush, he easily dealt with them using a Slumber Charm. Finding some strands of the detective’s hair, he prepared to do dream divination, thinking to himself: “Deduction, my good man.”
224: In the dream, Klein saw Zreal’s rotting corpse (described in detail as always. I might be starting to become numb to these descriptions, idk if this is a good or bad thing) in the sewers, confirming that he had already met his demise. At this point, Klein wasn’t disgusted by the sight, he had already seen more corpses than the average human would in 3 lifetimes. Using the materials on him, he forcefully entered the dream of one of the sleeping men.

The target revealed that they had been sent there by a high-ranking member of their gang named Meursault. After being done, Klein cleaned up any traces he left behind, bowed to the three sleeping men, before making his escape through a window, managing to lock it from the outside.

Heading to East Borough, Klein observed how the poor people there looked like living corpses, and how the police in the area treated them harshly. Arriving at his rented apartment, he divined the location of Zreal’s corpse before heading there, enduring the smell and the feeling of filth brought about by walking in the sewers. Finding the body that was way too rotten for someone who died only a few days before surrounded by rats munching on it, he failed at channeling the spirit, confirming that the matter involved Beyonders.
225: Making sure no one was tailing him, Klein returned to his home in Cherwood Borough. Ian passed by the next morning, surprised that the detective already made progress. He took the boy to the corpse’s location, asking him not to mention Sherlock Moriarty’s involvement when making a report to the police. With the job being done, Klein’s first request was for information about where he could get a gun and some bullets without needing a permit, receiving the answer that he should seek out Kaspars Kalinin at the Bravehearts Bar.

Elsewhere, Audrey was giving Fors Wall and Xio Derecha their reward for the previous mission (I think this was for the Qilangos thing? Can’t remember for sure), with the two promising to stay on the lookout for the Spectator and Apothecary formulas for Audrey and Glaint respectively (that was the guy who introduced Audrey to the two, they would search for mysticism-related stuff together).

Noticing some books that Audrey had laid out before their arrival, Xio and Fors asked to borrow them (they didn’t know Audrey had put them there deliberately). After arriving home, Xio found a piece of paper in her book that had some “Roselle symbols”, before reading the ancient Hermes written at the back of the paper out-loud. It was The Fool’s Honorific Name.
226: Klein was considering investing in something that was advertised in the newspapers when he heard an illusory voice. Heading above the gray fog, he saw the scene of Xio reading the name on the paper, deciding to only take action deep into the night to probe her reaction.

The woman only realized her mistake after she was done. Waiting in fear for an evil being to find her, she tried to calm herself down when she found no response. When Fors returned, her friend shared the experience with her, leaving the two frightened of this secret existence they had never heard of. They thought of seeking the protection of a church, but as they were of different faiths, that idea was quickly abandoned.

In the middle of the night, Klein went above the gray fog and, after deliberating over the matter for a while, attempted to pull Miss Justice’s friend to this other world. When her figure materialized at one of the seats, Xio was only able to get a glimpse of her surroundings before she was sent back. Klein was overjoyed as he confirmed more details about his abilities: he could establish at most one more connection with the current level of his spirituality, and he could pull Beyonders that are at most one Sequence higher than his own, though his success at doing so wasn’t guaranteed.

Xio, who wasn’t sure whether her very clear dream was brought about due to her fear or whether it was an actual response from “The Fool”, decided to get someone to exorcise her at a Beyonder gathering the following day just in case.
227: The next morning, Klein, who was missing the varied delicacies he could eat back on Earth, heard a knock on his door. It was Meursault, who had sent the people back at Zreal’s home (refer to the middle of chapter 224). He refused to talk inside and plainly stated that he wanted to hire Sherlock Moriarty to find Ian, believing that the detective already knew the boy. Klein first denied that before making it clear that this mission went against his principle of confidentiality, refusing to accept it no matter how high the man raised the price.

After he left, Klein, amidst a light drizzle, headed to the home of a man named Leppard, hoping to invest in the new transportation vehicle he was working on. After signing a non-disclosure agreement, he showed his invention, which he based on some manuscripts left behind by Emperor Roselle, to his potential investor. It was a car that worked with pedals. After explaining why this wasn’t something feasible, Klein instead shifted the man’s attention to working on a bike, claiming that it would benefit more people like the workers and businessmen.
After the deal was settled, Klein returned home. While looking in the mirror in his bathroom, he saw a pair of eyes to his side.
228: Barely dodging an arrow, Klein fought an immensely powerful black figure. It was thanks to his instincts as a Clown that he was able to dodge most of the attacks, though not without having to tank some of them. A clearer vision of the enemy revealed that it was Meursault, who was both agile and strong. Weakening his attacker by getting him to slam into furniture while also getting weakened by being sent flying through a table, Klein got a hold of a piece of paper and threw it as a projectile that stabbed right through the man’s throat.

Observing the damages to the place, he couldn’t help remembering that he could no longer claim reimbursement for that before descending into a fit of laughter. It was the only sound that reverberated in the entire house. When he finally calmed down, Klein used a dream to get some answers, finding out that Meursault was sent by the Intis ambassador to bring Ian Wright either alive or recently deceased so his spirit could be channeled. Though the gang-member didn’t know why the boy was wanted in the first place.
Finishing his communication with the dead man, Klein collected his Beyonder characteristic before considering what to do with the body.
229: Klein had three choices: clean up the scene and report this as legitimate self-defense, wait deep into the night and dispose of the corpse, or give up his current identity and flee before changing his name again. Thinking of all downsides to each of these choices, Klein was already inclined towards one of them, but used divination to confirm anyway.

Emptying Meursault’s pockets, Klein stabbed a dagger into his throat before hiding anything Beyonderrelated above the gray fog to interfere with any attempted divination (the gray fog interferes with divination). When he was done, Klein waited a bit so that by the time the police sent experts to investigate, the deceased’s spirit would have already lost the ability to give detailed information. Feeling like a professional at hiding his tracks, Klein compared himself to Moriarty and, after enough time had passed (he was counting the minutes while looking at his pocket watch), found the patrolling officers.

He told them that a criminal had attacked him and that he had accidentally stabbed him to death. When more officers arrived at his home, Klein truthfully gave his (fake) name, his occupation, proof he was renting this house, along with explaining the situation with Ian, Zreal, and Meursault’s gang. He even claimed to have tailed the man and found him talking to someone he addressed as “Mr. Ambassador”, saying that he knew how he looked but not his name.
Claiming his faith with the Church of Steam in order not to encounter the Nighthawks, Klein followed them to the police station.
230: In a Beyonder gathering, Xio was finally able to purchase the Sequence 8 Sheriff potion formula, she also set up a notice of a reward for someone skilled in exorcism. A believer of the sun responded, attempting a purification ritual. Klein, who was at the police station, was amused as he felt a strange warmth just as the cold of the cell was starting to seep into his body. Encouraging himself with the thought that matters regarding an ambassador would garner much more attention than a “puny” detective such as himself, and remembering the fact that he hid all signs of Beyonder involvement in his battle with Meursault, he waited until he was called to the interrogation room.

As soon as he sat down and the man opposite him started speaking, the oppressive force surrounding Klein made him immediately realize that he was talking to a Beyonder: A Sequence 7 Interrogator from the Arbiter pathway. He was made to identify the ambassador from a bunch of photographs before repeating what he knew about Ian Wright and assuring the Interrogator that everything he said was the truth.
After he was allowed to leave, Klein was taken to fill out some forms with the help of Jurgen Cooper (his neighbor whose grandmother has a cat), who had come to bail him out.
231: Klein paid the bail and was informed by Jurgen that he could come back for the money after the case was closed, but calculating his overall losses because of the damages to his home left him worried about his finances if he didn’t get back the bail. On their way back, the two agreed to work together in the future, starting with the contract for Klein’s bike investment.

As soon as he got home, he was invited by his neighbors who were also his landlords, Mr. and Mrs. Sammer. After he apologized for the mess, his hosts started inquiring about the situation (his answer was that it may have been a thief), before shifting their curiosity towards how much a private detective could earn. That led to Mrs. Sammer going on and on about what is considered a decent income and how one could live comfortably, and Klein found out that the Coim company Luke Sammer works at is specialized in anthracite and charcoal. The mention of her husband’s job got the woman to get back to her flaunting of their wealth. Klein was glad he at least didn’t have mean landlords.

He later decided to head to the Bravehearts bar, which Ian had mentioned, in the hopes of hiring a powerful Beyonder bodyguard for two reasons: taking advantage of his situation to come into contact with other Beyonders, and because he was genuinely afraid the ambassador would send someone more powerful next time. If the price was too high though, he thought of just blowing the copper whistle to get Mr. Azik’s help. Thinking about his situation, Klein found it comical that he, a Sequence 8 Beyonder, a vengeful evil spirit back from the dead, needed a bodyguard (he was really overestimating Sequence 8, and he considered himself an “evil” spirit? He had yet to experience the true cruelty of this world).
232: Back at the Beyonder gathering, the person who sold the Sheriff formula to Xio asked to speak to her in private and, after some deliberation, she agreed, though not before disguising herself completely. The man revealed that he also possessed the ingredients she would need, and that he came from a powerful organization that wanted to make a deal with her so their more “secretive” missions could be carried out by a bounty hunter instead. After making sure that she had the right to refuse any mission she found unsuitable for her, Xio agreed to the partnership.

As for Klein, he busied himself with buying replacements for everything that had been destroyed at his home, then he went to the bar to find Kaspars Kalinin with the code Ian had given him. He successfully purchased a revolver along with fifty rounds and asked about hiring a bodyguard that “exceeded human limitations.” Klein was sent to meet the man so that he could determine the danger of the mission before responding.
When entering the room, Klein used his Spirit Vision to find out that the Beyonder was playing cards with a bunch of zombies.
233: Acting as if he didn’t notice anything, Klein told the man, named Maric, that he had “offended a big shot who might have a country supporting him”. He was immediately kicked out. Seeing as this was the strongest Beyonder Kaspars knew, Klein just asked him to keep an eye out as he started to consider how he could deal with the matter all on his own.

Considering the fact that the ambassador’s target was Ian, Klein had the idea that he could shake him off by making it clear that he didn’t know the boy’s whereabouts. But after what happened, he couldn’t be sure that his enemy wouldn’t want to take revenge, which could be easily done by mentioning the fact that Meursault was a Beyonder, putting Sherlock Moriarty, who was able to kill him, in a difficult situation. Just thinking about all that made him have a strong desire to just kill the ambassador. Such an action wouldn’t bring him any psychological burden, as the other was the one who sent someone to kill Klein first. He also considered setting this as a mission for the Tarot Club.

Using dream divination, he was able to see the room Ian was in, but he was unable to pinpoint his exact location. The boy had even refused to leave anything with Klein, making it impossible to find him. Finally heading above the gray fog, he didn’t get a different answer, so he instead cast his sight onto a newly added crimson star.
